items.prompt:
Formal constructions use only:
A) A ruler and protractor
B) A compass and unmarked straightedge
C) A calculator
D) Graph paper
items.answer: B) A compass and unmarked straightedge

items.prompt:
Bisecting a segment also creates its:
A) Midpoint only
B) Perpendicular bisector
C) Parallel line
D) Angle bisector

steps: Equal arcs give the perpendicular bisector.

items.prompt:
May you use a protractor to measure angles in a formal construction?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only for right angles
D) Only once

steps: Only compass and straightedge are allowed.

items.prompt:
A compass reproduces equal lengths because:
A) It measures in inches
B) All radii of its circle are equal
C) It is marked
D) It uses a protractor
items.answer: B) All radii of its circle are equal

steps: A fixed opening gives equal radii.

items.prompt:
Which construction produces a line meeting another at a right angle?
A) Parallel line
B) Perpendicular line
C) Angle copy
D) Segment copy

steps: The perpendicular construction gives a right angle.

items.prompt:
The perpendicular bisector passes through a segment's:
A) Endpoint
B) Midpoint
C) Vertex
D) Center of a circle

steps: It bisects the segment at the midpoint.

items.prompt:
Why are intersecting equal-radius arcs used to bisect a segment?
A) They look nice
B) Their intersections are equidistant from both endpoints, lying on the perpendicular bisector
C) They measure length
D) They copy angles
items.answer: B) Their intersections are equidistant from both endpoints, lying on the perpendicular bisector

steps: Equidistant intersections define the perpendicular bisector.

items.prompt:
Which set lists only valid compass-and-straightedge constructions?
A) Measuring an angle, weighing a side
B) Copying an angle, bisecting a segment, drawing a parallel line
C) Reading coordinates, using a protractor
D) Timing and counting
items.answer: B) Copying an angle, bisecting a segment, drawing a parallel line
